draft.title: Culture shock
card: Culture shock is the confusion and stress some people feel in an unfamiliar culture. It can happen when daily habits, food, language or manners are very different from what they know.
Signs can include feeling anxious, tired, homesick or unsure how to act. People may also feel frustrated when familiar ways of doing things no longer work.
Culture shock is not a sign that something is wrong with the person or with the new culture. It is a normal reaction to a lot of unfamiliar things at once.
For most people it usually eases over time as they learn the local ways, make friends and get used to the routines. How long this takes differs from person to person.
draft.remember: Culture shock is a common reaction to the unfamiliar, and it usually eases with time.

a.q: Which situation is the best example of culture shock?
opts: A student feels anxious and homesick after moving to Japan
A student enjoys a holiday in Japan and plans a return trip
A student studies Japanese history from a library book
A student thinks Japanese customs are worse than her own
a.why: The student is stressed and unsettled by living in an unfamiliar culture, which is culture shock. Thinking customs are worse is a different idea, because it is a judgement about another culture and not a stress reaction.
a.clue: Look for stress caused by an unfamiliar way of life.

b.q: Tariq moved from Lebanon to Dubbo. In his first month he felt tired and confused by local manners. By month six he felt much more settled. What does this show about culture shock?
opts: It usually eases as people adjust to the new culture
It means the person was unsuited to living in Australia
It only affects people who dislike the new culture
It stays the same for as long as a person lives there
b.why: Tariq's confusion faded as he got used to local ways, which matches how culture shock usually eases. It does not mean he was unsuited to the move, because the card describes it as a normal reaction to many unfamiliar things at once.
b.clue: Compare how Tariq felt in month one with month six.

a.best: A student feels anxious and homesick after moving to Japan

b.best: It usually eases as people adjust to the new culture

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('usually'), while every distractor is absolute ('only affects', 'stays the same for as long as', 'means the person was unsuited'). A test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea.
